Everything in the order it is meant to be read. Each chapter and interlude is summed up in a sentence or two, so you can see the whole arc before committing to any of it, and find your place again later. Under each are a few of the ideas it introduces; every one of them has its own short page if you would rather wander than read straight through.

The argument in one line: ideas are compressed and filtered on their way to you; the filter is tuned for attention, not truth; here is what that does, and what could carry hard truths through anyway.

## Part I: The Pipeline

*How information moves from reality to people.*

### [[the-information-landscape|Chapter 1: The Information Landscape]]

How an idea gets from the world to you: five lossy hops (measurement, analysis, consensus, news, meme) and, at each one, a gate that throws most of it away on criteria that have nothing to do with truth.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[manufactured-injection|Manufactured injection]] · [[memetic-fitness|Memetic fitness]] · [[selection|Selection]] · [[transport|Transport]] · [[astrology|Astrology]] · [[framework|Framework]] · [[legibility|Legibility]] · [[option-space|Option space]]

### [[case-studies-and-three-realities|Chapter 2: Case Studies and Three Realities]]

Four real findings walked through the pipeline: power posing, arsenic-life, the Stanford Prison Experiment, astrology. Why a correction almost always loses to the myth it corrects, and why money, law, and nations play by different rules.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[three-realities|Three realities]] · [[scientists-say-x|'Scientists say X' headline]] · [[arsenic-life|Arsenic-life]] · [[astrology|Astrology]] · [[constitutive-regimes|Constitutive regimes]] · [[constitutive-transmission|Constitutive transmission]] · [[power-posing|Power posing]] · [[stanford-prison-experiment-corrective|Stanford Prison Experiment correctives]]

## Part II: Why It Has To Be Lossy (And Selective)

*The structural reasons compression and selection both operate.*

### [[info-time-limit|Chapter 3: The Human Time Budget]]

You get a tablespoon of weeks, and only a few focused hours in each. How much an hour can carry depends on what you already know and what you want to spend it on, and both can be trained.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[receiver-budget|Receiver budget]] · [[power-posing|Power posing]]

### [[optionality-vs-access|Chapter 4: Optionality vs. Access]]

Why the most powerful version of anything (a code library, the Latin Mass, a statute, a physics paper) is the hardest to use, and why the easy version always loses something. One trade-off, five domains.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[brief-history-of-time|A Brief History of Time]] · [[cost-asymmetry|Cost asymmetry]] · [[default-setting|Defaults]] · [[framework|Framework]] · [[framework-pricing|Framework pricing]] · [[latin-mass-vs-vernacular|Latin Mass vs. vernacular liturgy]] · [[calculus-notation|Leibniz's dy/dx and the British lag]] · [[matplotlib-vs-seaborn|matplotlib vs. seaborn]]

### [[complexity-virality-tradeoff|Chapter 5: The Complexity / Virality Trade-off]]

Why the easy-to-share version of an idea always wins over the accurate one: every retelling costs the listener effort and loses a little, and across a big enough network the losses compound until only the slogan is left.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[complex-form|Complex form]] · [[complexity-ceiling|Complexity ceiling]] · [[compressed-form|Compressed form]] · [[handle-ability|Handle-ability]] · [[manipulation-surface|Manipulation surface]] · [[three-layer-message|The three-layer message]] · [[transport|Transport]] · [[brief-history-of-time|A Brief History of Time]]

### [[selection-as-other-engine|Chapter 5b: Selection As The Other Engine]]

Ideas don't just get garbled as they spread; most never spread at all. Every reader, editor, and algorithm is a gate with criteria, and because criteria can be set, this is the half of the machine someone can steer.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[algorithm-as-selection-engine|Algorithm as selection engine]] · [[conformity|Conformity]] · [[false-consensus-rational-agents|False consensus among rational agents]] · [[meme-ecosystem-competition|Meme ecosystem competition]] · [[neutral-drift-baseline|Neutral drift baseline]] · [[replicator-ontology|Replicator ontology]] · [[arsenic-life|Arsenic-life]] · [[complexity-ceiling|Complexity ceiling]]

### [[medium-and-manipulation|Interlude: The Medium]]

A medium is not the wire; it is the set of rules for what wins. This note works out the three things a medium does to every gate, defines manipulation as tuning a gate against truth, and asks which media let truth survive.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[option-space|Option space]]

### [[truth-compression-and-when-each-wins|Chapter 5c: Truth, Compression, and When Each Wins]]

Simplifying a claim doesn't make it false. It strips the instructions for reading it, and what happens next depends on which instructions the reader substitutes: the truth survives, flips, or stops mattering. Which of the three wins is chosen by the gate, not the compression.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[interpretive-latitude|Interpretive latitude]] · [[truth-compression-regimes|Truth-compression regimes]] · [[compressed-form-as-authority|Compressed form becoming authoritative]] · [[covid-mask-guidance|COVID mask guidance]] · [[myth-dilution|Myth dilution at scale]] · [[power-posing|Power posing]] · [[pseudo-context|Pseudo-context]] · [[reflective-vs-intuitive-belief|Reflective vs. intuitive belief]]

## Part III: The Bridge Zone

*Where complex specialist knowledge gets transformed (and often destroyed) on its way to mass audiences.*

### [[bridge-zone-distortion|Chapter 6: Where It All Gets Fucked Up]]

Between the scientists and you sits a crowd paid to make findings land: journalists, popularizers, influencers, AI summarizers. They answer to audiences, not to the field, so they reshape on purpose. This is where the eggs-are-killing-you whiplash comes from.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[pseudo-context|Pseudo-context]] · [[technology-vs-medium|Technology vs. medium]] · [[scientists-say-x|'Scientists say X' headline]] · [[brief-history-of-time|A Brief History of Time]] · [[bridge-zone|Bridge zone]] · [[covid-mask-guidance|COVID mask guidance]] · [[credibility-weighting|Credibility weighting]] · [[monetary-policy-press|Monetary policy in the financial press]]

### [[emotional-memetics|Chapter 7: Emotional Memetics As The Floor]]

Why the furious post spreads and the careful one doesn't, even though most people say they'd prefer the reverse. Once a network is large and its gates reward engagement, what reliably travels settles at raw emotion. Includes a head-on answer to Mercier's claim that people aren't that easy to manipulate.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[epistemic-vigilance|Epistemic vigilance]] · [[justification-market|Justification market]] · [[open-vigilance|Open vigilance]] · [[paradox-of-virality|Paradox of virality]] · [[reflective-vs-intuitive-belief|Reflective vs. intuitive belief]] · [[bridge-zone|Bridge zone]] · [[compressed-form|Compressed form]] · [[conformity|Conformity]]

### [[myths-scale-and-bureaucracy|Interlude: Myths at Scale]]

Why a story big enough for a billion people to share is too vague to mean one thing, why that splits the group, and why every large network grows institutions to hold the full version and re-teach it.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[interpretive-latitude|Interpretive latitude]] · [[myth-dilution|Myth dilution at scale]] · [[network-segmentation|Network segmentation]]

## Part IV: A Way Through

*Hypothesis territory. Rebuilt around integration between networks that don't share preconditions.*

### [[preservation-vs-training|Chapter 8: Preservation vs. Training]]

Why keeping knowledge alive takes two separate institutions, one to preserve the full form and one to train people who can read it, and why losing the training side is the more dangerous and less reversible failure.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[capture-asymmetry|Capture asymmetry]] · [[institutional-decay-rates|Differential decay rates]] · [[preservation-vs-training-pair|Preservation vs. training]] · [[capture-taxonomy|Capture taxonomy]] · [[complex-form|Complex form]] · [[consumer-key-vs-surface-capture|Consumer-key vs. surface capture]] · [[decompression-on-demand|Decompression on demand]] · [[justification-market|Justification market]]

### [[intersubjective-truth|Chapter 8b: Intersubjective Truth]]

Money, law, and nations are true because enough people agree. This note works out what happens to that kind of truth in a pipeline that reaches into everyone's heads: spreading it is part of making it, it can't be corrected only forked, and it now moves faster than the institutions that steady it.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[constitutive-regimes|Constitutive regimes]] · [[constitutive-transmission|Constitutive transmission]] · [[reification|Reification]] · [[truth-generators|Truth generators]]

### [[integration-problem|Chapter 9: The Integration Problem]]

How real knowledge crosses between groups that don't share training or trust: the people who can translate, the institutions that protect them, why more connection can make things worse, and five practical limits on the whole project.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[curation-layer|Curation layer]] · [[echo-chambers-vs-bubbles|Echo chambers vs. bubbles]] · [[inverted-u|Inverted-U relationship]] · [[zollman-effect|The Zollman effect]] · [[common-law-courts|Common-law courts as a curation institution]] · [[constitutive-regimes|Constitutive regimes]] · [[myth-dilution|Myth dilution at scale]] · [[network-segmentation|Network segmentation]]

### [[political-economy-of-attention|Chapter 10: Political Economy of Attention]]

Why the feeds that decide what you see are tuned to hold your attention rather than inform you, why there's no villain to blame for it, and why the same trap shows up on public blockchains.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[cost-shifting|Cost-shifting from producers to consumers]] · [[creation-cheap-review-expensive|Creation cheap / review expensive]] · [[credibility-weighting|Credibility weighting]] · [[engagement-equilibrium|Engagement-maximization as a captured equilibrium]] · [[out-competition-of-carriers|Out-competition of institutional carriers in attention markets]] · [[self-vs-external-capture|Self-capture vs. external capture]] · [[superspreader-dynamics|Superspreader dynamics]] · [[orwell-huxley-axis|The Orwell/Huxley axis]]

### [[ai-as-new-node|Chapter 11: AI as a New Kind of Node]]

What changes when one company controls what an AI learned from, what it was rewarded for, how it's configured, who can afford it, and the writing itself; and why that makes it either the best study aid ever built or the tightest grip on what people know.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[compressed-form-as-authority|Compressed form becoming authoritative]] · [[decompression-on-demand|Decompression on demand]] · [[llm-design-moment-collapse|LLM as collapsed selection-design moment]] · [[ai-benchmarks|AI benchmarks as milestones]] · [[algorithm-as-selection-engine|Algorithm as selection engine]] · [[capture-asymmetry|Capture asymmetry]] · [[capture-taxonomy|Capture taxonomy]] · [[constitutive-transmission|Constitutive transmission]]

### [[capture-taxonomy|Interlude: Capture]]

One definition of capture and three questions to ask of any case: which part of the system was rigged, who rigged it (an outsider, the institution itself, or both), and how hard it is to undo. Rigging what people read with is worse than rigging what they see.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[capture-asymmetry|Capture asymmetry]] · [[capture-taxonomy|Capture taxonomy]] · [[consumer-key-vs-surface-capture|Consumer-key vs. surface capture]] · [[corpus-capture|Corpus capture]] · [[deployment-capture|Deployment capture]] · [[objective-capture|Objective capture]] · [[self-vs-external-capture|Self-capture vs. external capture]]

### [[infrastructure-for-integration|Chapter 12: Infrastructure for Integration]]

Design rules for institutions that keep hard-won knowledge alive in an attention economy they cannot beat: fund them outside the engagement market, protect what gets installed in people and models first, build them to work under distrust, and own any AI they use.

*Ideas you will meet:* [[curation-layer|Curation layer]] · [[funding-decoupling|Funding decoupling from attention markets]] · [[llm-as-capability-extender|LLM as capability extender]] · [[survivable-polarization|Survivable polarization]] · [[survival-not-victory|Survival, not victory]] · [[work-of-generations|Work of generations]] · [[capture-taxonomy|Capture taxonomy]] · [[common-law-courts|Common-law courts as a curation institution]]

## Side roads

Notes that work one question through at more depth than the chapters do. Read one when a chapter sends you there, or when its question is the one you came with.

- [[transport-vs-selection|Transport vs. Selection]]: Why ideas get simpler as they spread: not because each retelling loses a little, but because at every step something chooses which version travels. Transport is a cost; selection is a choice; only a choice can be steered.
- [[bridge-nodes-and-versatile-expertise|Bridge Nodes and Versatile Expertise]]: Who can carry a hard idea from one field into another? Not a generalist. A deep specialist who has also learned to suspend their own frame, because the four ways expertise fails are the same thing that polarizes a network.
- [[thinking-inside-frameworks|Thinking Inside Frameworks]]: The tools you think with (languages, forms, metrics, models) filter an idea before you say a word. They do it by making some thoughts cheap and others expensive, the effect is a lean and not a cage, and the trouble grows when the world gets rebuilt to match the tool.
